top_story: Saudi Arabia’s move to execute a man for protest-related acts allegedly committed when he was 15 underscores a broader regional pattern in which security-first governance overrides protections for juveniles, dissenters, and due process. Together, these developments point to a hardening climate in which coercion is not only intensifying against civilians but also increasingly visible to foreign witnesses, raising the diplomatic stakes without yet constraining the actors involved.
